item.title: This founder cracked firefighting — now he’s creating an AI gold mine
item.description: The nozzle is just the beginning – what company founder Sunny Sethi calls "the muscle on the ground.”

item.title: ChatGPT is pulling answers from Elon Musk’s Grokipedia
item.description: Information from the conservative-leaning, AI-generated encyclopedia developed by Elon Musk’s xAI is beginning to appear in answers from ChatGPT.

item.title: Humans& thinks coordination is the next frontier for AI, and they’re building a model to prove it
item.description: Humans&, a new startup founded by alumni of Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, xAI, and Google DeepMind, is building the next generation of foundation models for collaboration, not chat.

item.title: Science fiction writers, Comic-Con say goodbye to AI
item.description: Some of the major players in science fiction and pop culture are taking firmer stances against generative AI.

item.title: Arctic Weather Satellite paves way for constellation observation
item.description: Already recognized for its excellence and even adopted for operational weather forecasting, the European Space Agency's Arctic Weather Satellite has now fulfilled its most important role. This small prototype mission has succeeded in paving the way for a new constellation of similar satellites, known as EPS-Sterna.

item.title: Chandra catalog now contains 1.3 million X-ray detections across the sky
item.description: Like a recording artist who has had a long career, NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory has a "back catalog" of cosmic recordings that is impossible to replicate. To access these X-ray tracks, or observations, the ultimate compendium has been developed: the Chandra Source Catalog (CSC).

item.title: A new study of lunar rocks suggests Earth's water might not have come from meteorites
item.description: For a long time, scientists assumed that Earth's water was delivered by asteroids and comets billions of years ago. This coincided with the Late Heavy Bombardment (ca. 4.1 to 3.8 billion years ago), a period when planets and bodies in the solar system experienced a much higher rate of impacts.

item.title: Apple will reportedly unveil its Gemini-powered Siri assistant in February
item.description: We’re about to get our first real look at the results of the recently announced AI partnership between Apple and Google.

item.title: A new look at trends in human deaths due to climate extremes
item.description: A new study of climate extremes since 1988 finds that many regions have seen increases in deaths due to floods, storms and extreme temperatures. In human terms, the harm comes not just from deaths, but also from lost labor and property damage. (And this doesn't consider damage to species and ecosystems.) A new look at trends and outliers has been published in Geophysical Research Letters.

item.title: The Mount Maunganui tragedy reminds us landslides are NZ's deadliest natural hazard
item.description: The tragic events in the Bay of Plenty this week are a stark reminder that landslides remain the deadliest of the many natural hazards New Zealand faces. A large landslide swept through the Mount Maunganui Beachside Holiday Park at the base of Mauao, triggering a major rescue and recovery operation that will continue through the weekend.

item.title: A decade of Star Trek-themed fart jokes: The Greatest Generation podcast turns 10
item.description: How two podcasters turned a Star Trek side project into a full-time career.

item.title: Cleaner air is (inadvertently) harming the Great Barrier Reef
item.description: Air pollution is now recognized as one of the greatest threats to human health, contributing to an estimated 4.2 million premature deaths in 2019, according to the World Health Organization.
